battery.finding: 72 % is set by protecting a full hour of the high-band black-start service load. Restarting one L2 unit first and pausing cryo inside the sealed hold (R1) protects 665 kWh nominal (33 %; 16-92 % across the bands, the high end being a cold restart with 1.5x uncertainty and a 12 h L3 start). Keeping one unit in warm standby cuts the restart to ~25 kWh. A separate 2.3 t restart pack (R2) frees the whole main pack for ride-through and removes the single-pack common mode. At 1C an 800 Wh/kg pack delivers 2 MW, below the 3.4 MW coast load: the ride-through is power-limited, loads must shed to the discharge limit within seconds, and ride-through hours are an energy bound only.

buffer.finding: With the OPEN planning loads (the owner's 4.8 MW case) C-lean has 0.53 MW of surplus at BOL nominal and none at EOL (0.01 MW): a 10 s engagement every 10 min recharges in ~7 min at BOL and never at EOL, at the high band or after a unit trip. On known loads alone the surplus is 1.9 MW BOL / 1.4 MW EOL nominal. Running all four units adds 1.75 MW but removes the hot standby. The buffer is sized by ~21 MW of discharge power and 10 s of energy: ~14 t of high-power Li cells or ~13 t of supercapacitors (supercapacitors win only below ~3 s), not 2.4 t. Engagement heat beyond the WARM spare needs a ~0.1-1 GJ thermal buffer.

thermal_closure.rule: A state closes only if every active circuit passes at the band; unused area elsewhere gets no credit without a temperature and transport path.
thermal_closure.finding: No state closes at every band. In coast LOW fails at the high band (1.10 MW against 1.07 MW usable) and in every band once a blade circuit is lost; WARM fails at the high band once the OPEN planning loads land on it, and an engagement fails WARM without a thermal buffer. In burns the working doctrine fits WARM at the nominal band (5.0 MW with planning), but L1's own conversion waste (~900 K) has no radiator in the production geometry at all: a gap Phase II did not count. L2 has no sink in burns or while the channels refill.

shielding.blocker: BLOCKER: no validated radiation-transport tool (MCNP/OpenMC with evaluated nuclear data, coupled n-gamma, the real geometry incl. blade scatter and streaming through the riser and hatch penetrations) is available in this environment. Every shield mass here is a simplified exponential-attenuation estimate. Shielding stays OPEN; nothing here establishes crew safety.
shielding.finding: Shield mass and volume now agree by construction (rho 1.9 t/m3 for LiH + 6 % W; Phase II used 1.6 and a 2.8 m3 envelope that cannot hold 27.9 t). The nominal unit needs ~15 t shadow + ~22 t blade slab = ~37 t, more than Phase II. The He-3 tanks on the outer ring sit ~25-30 deg off the district axis, outside a 12.5 deg shadow cone; three units would deposit up to ~16 kW (upper bound, all of it absorbed) into tanks whose 3 K stage lifts ~118 W in total; even 1 % reaching the 3 K stage exceeds it. Either the shadow widens to ~30 deg (doesn't fit a 3.2 m bay) or the tanks get their own shadow: a coupling the district must solve. Shutdown gamma keeps crew out of line of sight for weeks; servicing is robotic.

thermal_architectures.finding: Under the working doctrine the burn heat pumps vanish in every architecture (WARM 3.6 MW fits 6.0 MW usable). What remains is L1's own 900 K rejection and L2's missing sink in burns. C and F give L2 a 550 K sink by taking ~23-37 m from the forward end of the hot blades (2.1-3.3 GW of the 3.6 GW hot allowance, to be confirmed against the drive's hot budget): L2 then runs through burns and the burn-to-coast gap disappears. D does the same inside today's WARM blades for one unit but leaves the 440 K part too small at the high band. Thermal storage only works per engagement.

l1.finding: Reduce demand first: the working doctrine takes L1 from ~150 MW to ~45 MW nominal, and the OPEN hot-loop pumps are 90 % of what is left. Heat-pipe hot blades (a propulsion-interface choice) take L1 to ~5 MW; if L2 also carries the ship in burns (thermal options C/F) L1 shrinks to ~0.6 MW of drive-specific loads. Thermal conversion from the hot loop is the only non-speculative option; inductive and direct conversion stay SPECULATIVE and are not credited.

rows.name: C-lean all four partial
rows.strategy: all four at ~75 %, no standby (faster response, more wear)

rows.name: C-lean 3+1 + essential-only redundancy
rows.strategy: N+1 only for essentials (0.45 MW): proactive defense sheds on a trip

l2.finding: At end of life a 1.75 MWe unit gives ~1.58 MW, so C-lean needs three of four units for proactive defense: it is N+1 with no margin and the most likely to fall short (18 % over 3 years at u = 0.05 with repair, 3 % lasting). Fewer, larger units with one unit per blade do better (2+1 x 2.66: 9 % / 2 %; 2 x 100 %: 5 % / 1 %; 4+1 x 1.33: 9 % / 1.5 %), at masses within 15 % (233-266 t nominal) because every unit carries its own shield. Moving C-lean unit 4 to another blade does not help: four units on three blades always share a header. Without ORU repair the lasting-shortfall probability rises about fivefold. Every option has ~0 surplus at EOL once the OPEN planning loads arrive: running capacity should be ~6 MWe, not 5.3. Service life (20 years) is not an unserviced mission: units are swapped between missions.

rows.notes: each unit its own shadow + blade slab; fits a 3.2 m bay; outer-ring He-3 tanks outside the cone (OPEN)

district.finding: Individual shields stay lightest and fit. A shared shadow wall across the M2 forward face is the only option that also shades the tank farm and the keel-lane traffic; it weighs about as much as four slabs and turns M1-M2 into a closed district with controlled penetrations. Recommended research direction: individual shields + a partial tank-facing wall, pending transport.

transition.finding: A drive trip at velocity leaves the ship without proactive defense for ~0.3-4 h, set by the OPEN channel refill. That is not SAFE even though the refuge carries the crew: it is a mission and hull risk proportional to dust flux x gap. Options C/F (or D for one unit) remove it.

missions.correction: Phase II used the 7.55 d / 6.97 AU ramp; the flown profile is power-limited: the first burn takes 9.99 d over 13.26 AU, later burns are shorter as the ship lightens.
missions.finding: 0.016 c is a capability. Inside ~200 AU a 0.008 c cruise costs months, not years, and saves ~60 % of the propellant, an 8x lower defense load and an 8x lower dust fluence per year. Beyond ~500 AU only 0.012-0.016 c keeps round trips inside 36 months.

decisions.question: Adopt R1 (L2-first restart, cryo paused in the sealed hold) as the black-start study basis; keep canon step 2 until decided
Size the defense buffer by discharge power (supercapacitors) and adopt a 10 s / 10 min engagement duty as the planning case
Open a radiator research variant for a 550 K section (thermal option F); production stays unchanged (DR-03)
Ask propulsion for heat-pipe hot blades (removes the OPEN hot-loop pumps from L1)
Move the L2 study reference from C-lean 3+1 x 1.75 to 2+1 x 2.66-3.0 MWe (one unit per blade); keep 4+1 x 1.33 as the alternative
Commission a radiation-transport assessment before any shield or district decision
Treat the He-3 tank shadow as a district requirement (tank-facing wall or tank shields)
Use modular 4-person ECLSS units for the one-ring case
Make cruise speed a per-mission choice (0.008 c inside 200 AU)
